text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Thursday.

LONDON - Rising continental markets and strong gilts dragged shares off their lows late in the session, after a day dogged by weakness in drug stocks and lacking the usual Wall Street stimulus as New York took its annual Thanksgiving break. The FTSE 100 index closed up 1.0 point at 4,050.2.

FRANKFURT - Shares powered ahead to new record highs, boosted by strength in the German bond market and a firmer dollar, which helped shares in stocks of many German exporters climb to new ground. The DAX index of 30 top shares ended bourse trade at a record closing high of 2,817.49 points up 20.46 points. Later, in the last half hour of post-bourse dealings, the IBIS DAX lept ahead even further, ending at 2,829.68 points.

PARIS - Shares closed with a surprise run up, as the market squeezed higher ahead of the expiry of November futures and options contracts. Traders said the cash market, which had been looking to consolidate, was essentially pulled by the futures pit. The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended up 19.54 points or 0.86 percent at 2,290.31.

ZURICH - Shares ended with an strong recovery of one percent after a sharp slump on Wednesday. Initial caution due to the holiday in the United States and rumours of Roche takeover plans was brushed aside. One dealer warned fears of a correction on Wall Street persist, adding the market may move sideways. The all-share SPI added 19.98 points to 2,480.76.

TOKYO - Tokyo's benchmark Nikkei average closed sharply lower due mostly to profit-taking of recent, high-flying blue chips and intermittent bouts of futures-linked selling. The Nikkei 225 closed 309.74 points, or 1.45 percent, lower at 21,035.54.

HONG KONG - The Hang Seng index posted its biggest point decline since July, ending sharply lower after futures-linked volatility drove it to an early record high before prices succumbed to profit-taking. The Hang Seng index whipsawed in a range of 444 points before closing the day down 220.19 points at 13,310.76.

SYDNEY - Shares finished higher with gains underpinned by a stronger resource sector which was buoyed by firmer metal prices and takeover activity in the gold sector. The All Ordinaries index, closed 9.6 points firmer at 2,386.3. Turnover was lifted by a heavy activity in the gold sector following bids for Papua New Guinea gold miner Highlands Gold and Placer Pacific by Canada's Placer Dome Inc.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended weak in fairly active trade as the market tried to catch up on trade lost due to repeated breakdowns in the electronic trading system since Monday. The overall index shed 35.3 points to 6,714.1, the industrial index lost 51 points to 8,000.4 points and the gold index was off 37 points to 1,526.7 points.
